title: ICA-Based Artifact Removal
text: Independent Component Analysis (ICA) blind source separation technique commonly used identify remove artifacts electrophysiological recordings. Artifacts eye blinks, eye movements, muscle activity, heartbeat contamination can isolated independent components removed without discarding entire channels epochs. PhysioPreprocess provides two ICA workflows: Built-ICA (icaDecompose() / icaRemove()): self-contained FastICA implementation additional dependencies. fastICA-based (runICA() / removeICAComponents()): wrapper around fastICA package users prefer interface. vignette walks approaches.

title: ICA-Based Artifact Removal
code: library(PhysioCore) library(PhysioPreprocess)

title: ICA-Based Artifact Removal
text: simulate multi-channel EEG recording containing mixture neural sources artifact sources.
code: set.seed(123) n_time <- 2560 n_channels <- 16 sr <- 256  # Simulate 10 seconds of data with injected artifacts raw_data <- matrix(rnorm(n_time * n_channels), nrow = n_time, ncol = n_channels)  # Inject a simulated eye-blink artifact into frontal channels blink <- dnorm(seq(-3, 3, length.out = 100), mean = 0, sd = 1) * 50 blink_onset <- 500 raw_data[blink_onset:(blink_onset + 99), 1:2] <-   raw_data[blink_onset:(blink_onset + 99), 1:2] + blink  pe <- PhysioExperiment(   assays = list(raw = raw_data),   colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(     label = paste0("Ch", seq_len(n_channels)),     type = rep("EEG", n_channels)   ),   samplingRate = sr ) pe

title: ICA-Based Artifact Removal
text: built-ICA implementation uses FastICA algorithm PCA-based whitening. requires additional packages.

title: ICA-Based Artifact Removal
text: icaDecompose() separates multi-channel signal statistically independent components. component represents source signal maximally non-Gaussian. result list containing: components: independent component time courses (time x components). mixing: mixing matrix mapping components channels. unmixing: unmixing matrix mapping channels components. object: updated PhysioExperiment ICA decomposition stored metadata(object)$ica (components, mixing/unmixing matrices, column means).
code: ica_result <- icaDecompose(pe, n_components = 16, method = "fastica") str(ica_result$mixing) str(ica_result$unmixing)  # The ICA decomposition lives in the object's metadata (not as an assay, since the # number of components need not equal the number of channels). pe_ica <- ica_result$object names(S4Vectors::metadata(pe_ica)$ica) dim(S4Vectors::metadata(pe_ica)$ica$components)

title: ICA-Based Artifact Removal
text: Identifying components represent artifacts typically done visual inspection component time courses topographies. Components corresponding eye blinks tend show large, brief deflections concentrated frontal electrodes.
code: # Examine the mixing matrix to see each component's spatial pattern # Columns of the mixing matrix show the contribution of each component # to each channel mixing <- ica_result$mixing print(round(mixing[, 1:4], 3))  # A component heavily weighted on frontal channels (Ch1, Ch2) with # characteristic blink morphology is likely an eye-blink artifact

title: ICA-Based Artifact Removal
text: artifact components identified, icaRemove() zeros components reconstructs signal remaining components.
code: # Remove component 1 (identified as eye-blink artifact) pe_clean <- icaRemove(pe_ica, components = c(1), output_assay = "ica_cleaned")  # The cleaned data is stored in the "ica_cleaned" assay SummarizedExperiment::assayNames(pe_clean)

title: ICA-Based Artifact Removal
text: fastICA package installed, can use runICA() removeICAComponents() wrapper functions. provide simpler interface delegates computation fastICA package.

title: ICA-Based Artifact Removal
text: result list : S: Source matrix (time x components). : Mixing matrix (channels x components). W: Unmixing matrix (components x channels).
code: ica_result2 <- runICA(pe, n_components = 10) dim(ica_result2$S) dim(ica_result2$A) dim(ica_result2$W)

title: ICA-Based Artifact Removal
text: identifying artifact components, use removeICAComponents() reconstruct cleaned signal.
code: pe_clean2 <- removeICAComponents(pe, ica_result2, remove_components = c(1, 3)) SummarizedExperiment::assayNames(pe_clean2)

title: ICA-Based Artifact Removal
text: running ICA, often helpful identify handle bad channels. Bad channels can degrade ICA decomposition quality introduce noise may spread across multiple components.
code: # Detect channels with abnormally high or low variance bad_zscore <- detectBadChannels(pe, method = "zscore", threshold = 3)  # Detect channels with low correlation to neighbors bad_corr <- detectBadChannels(pe, method = "correlation", threshold = 0.4)  # Detect flatline channels bad_flat <- detectBadChannels(pe, method = "flatline", threshold = 0.01)  # Combine results bad_all <- unique(c(bad_zscore, bad_corr, bad_flat)) print(bad_all)

title: ICA-Based Artifact Removal
text: Bad channels can replaced interpolated values neighboring channels ICA decomposition.
code: # Interpolation borrows from the remaining good channels, so at least one channel # must be left unflagged. On this synthetic noise the correlation detector can flag # most channels; interpolate a subset that still leaves good channels. n_ch <- ncol(pe) to_interp <- if (length(bad_all) >= n_ch) utils::head(bad_all, n_ch - 1L) else bad_all if (length(to_interp) > 0) {   pe_interp <- interpolateBadChannels(pe, bad_channels = to_interp,                                        method = "average") }

title: ICA-Based Artifact Removal
text: typical preprocessing pipeline EEG data incorporating ICA artifact removal follows order: Highpass filter remove slow drifts (e.g., 1 Hz cutoff). Notch filter remove power line noise. Detect interpolate bad channels. Run ICA cleaned, filtered data. Identify remove artifact components. Re-reference average reference. Epoch data around events interest. Baseline correct epoch.
code: # Step 1: Highpass filter at 1 Hz pe_hp <- butterworthFilter(pe, low = 1, type = "high")  # Step 2: Notch filter at 50 Hz pe_notch <- notchFilter(pe_hp, freq = 50)  # Step 3: Detect and interpolate bad channels bad <- detectBadChannels(pe_notch, method = "zscore") if (length(bad) > 0) {   pe_notch <- interpolateBadChannels(pe_notch, bad_channels = bad) }  # Step 4: Run ICA ica <- icaDecompose(pe_notch, method = "fastica") pe_ica <- ica$object  # Step 5: Remove artifact components (after visual inspection) pe_clean <- icaRemove(pe_ica, components = c(1))  # Step 6: Re-reference to average pe_ref <- rereference(pe_clean, ref_type = "average")

title: ICA-Based Artifact Removal
text: number ICA components extract affects decomposition quality: components: Artifact neural sources may mixed within component, making clean separation impossible. many components: Components may capture noise rather meaningful sources, decomposition may become unstable. common practice use number components channels, reduce dimensionality first via PCA (icaDecompose() internally whitening step).
code: # Use all channels ica_full <- icaDecompose(pe, n_components = n_channels)  # Use a reduced number (e.g., for rank-deficient data after average reference) ica_reduced <- icaDecompose(pe, n_components = 12)

title: Signal Preprocessing Guide

title: Signal Preprocessing Guide
code: library(PhysioCore) library(PhysioPreprocess)

title: Signal Preprocessing Guide
text: begin constructing PhysioExperiment object simulated EEG-like data. object holds time--channels matrix primary assay along channel metadata sampling rate.
code: set.seed(42) n_time <- 2560 n_channels <- 10 sr <- 256  # Simulate 10 seconds of data at 256 Hz raw_data <- matrix(rnorm(n_time * n_channels), nrow = n_time, ncol = n_channels)  pe <- PhysioExperiment(   assays = list(raw = raw_data),   colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(     label = c("Fp1", "Fp2", "F3", "F4", "C3", "C4", "P3", "P4", "O1", "O2"),     type = rep("EEG", n_channels)   ),   samplingRate = sr ) pe

title: Signal Preprocessing Guide
text: PhysioPreprocess offers several filtering functions removing unwanted frequency components recorded signals.

title: Signal Preprocessing Guide
text: simplest filter moving average, smooths signal averaging sliding window. useful quick noise reduction offers limited frequency selectivity.
code: pe_ma <- filterSignals(pe, window = 5)

title: Signal Preprocessing Guide
text: Butterworth filter infinite impulse response (IIR) filter widely used physiological signal processing. provides maximally flat magnitude response passband supports lowpass, highpass, bandpass, bandstop configurations. Zero-phase forward-backward filtering applied automatically via signal::filtfilt().
code: # Bandpass filter between 1 and 40 Hz (common for EEG) pe_bp <- butterworthFilter(pe, low = 1, high = 40, type = "pass")  # Highpass filter at 0.5 Hz to remove slow drift pe_hp <- butterworthFilter(pe, low = 0.5, type = "high",                            output_assay = "highpass")  # Lowpass filter at 30 Hz pe_lp <- butterworthFilter(pe, high = 30, type = "low",                            output_assay = "lowpass")

title: Signal Preprocessing Guide
text: Finite impulse response (FIR) filters offer linear phase guaranteed stability. require higher order Butterworth filters transition bandwidth predictable frequency response.
code: pe_fir <- firFilter(pe, low = 1, high = 40, order = 100, type = "pass")

title: Signal Preprocessing Guide
text: Power line interference (50 Hz Europe/Asia, 60 Hz Americas) common artifact electrophysiological recordings. notch filter removes fundamental frequency optionally harmonics.
code: # Remove 50 Hz power line noise pe_notch <- notchFilter(pe, freq = 50)  # Remove 60 Hz and its second harmonic pe_notch60 <- notchFilter(pe, freq = 60, harmonics = 2)

title: Signal Preprocessing Guide
text: Changing sampling rate sometimes necessary combining datasets recorded different rates reducing data size storage.

title: Signal Preprocessing Guide
text: resample() function converts data target sampling rate. Three interpolation methods available: linear interpolation (fast, adequate cases), spline interpolation (smoother), FFT-based resampling (preserves frequency content).
code: # Downsample from 256 Hz to 128 Hz pe_128 <- resample(pe, target_rate = 128, method = "linear")  # Upsample with spline interpolation pe_512 <- resample(pe, target_rate = 512, method = "spline")

title: Signal Preprocessing Guide
text: downsampling factor integer, decimate() applies anti-aliasing lowpass filter subsampling prevent spectral aliasing.
code: # Decimate by a factor of 2 (256 Hz -> 128 Hz) pe_dec <- decimate(pe, factor = 2)

title: Signal Preprocessing Guide
text: integer-factor upsampling, interpolate() inserts new samples using specified interpolation method.
code: # Upsample by a factor of 2 (256 Hz -> 512 Hz) pe_up <- interpolate(pe, factor = 2, method = "spline")

title: Signal Preprocessing Guide
text: Re-referencing changes reference electrode EEG data. choice reference affects spatial interpretation important preprocessing decision.

title: Signal Preprocessing Guide
text: average reference subtracts mean channels time point. common choice high-density EEG approximates reference-free measure.
code: pe_avg <- rereference(pe, ref_type = "average") getCurrentReference(pe_avg)

title: Signal Preprocessing Guide
text: single electrode can serve reference. Common choices include Cz, nose, mastoid electrode.
code: pe_c3 <- rereference(pe, ref_type = "channel", ref_channels = "C3")

title: Signal Preprocessing Guide
text: Averaging two electrodes (e.g., linked mastoids) provides symmetric reference.
code: # Assuming M1 and M2 channels exist # pe_linked <- rereference(pe, ref_type = "channels", #                          ref_channels = c("M1", "M2"))

title: Signal Preprocessing Guide
text: re-referencing, reference information stored object metadata can queried.
code: getCurrentReference(pe_avg) isAverageReferenced(pe_avg)

title: Signal Preprocessing Guide
text: Slow drifts DC offsets common electrophysiological recordings. Detrending removes trends without altering faster signal components.

title: Signal Preprocessing Guide
text: detrendSignals() function supports mean removal, linear detrending, polynomial detrending.
code: # Remove the mean (DC offset) pe_mean <- detrendSignals(pe, method = "mean")  # Remove a linear trend pe_linear <- detrendSignals(pe, method = "linear")  # Remove a quadratic trend pe_poly <- detrendSignals(pe, method = "polynomial", order = 2)

title: Signal Preprocessing Guide
text: detrendSignal() function filters-advanced.R provides simpler interface linear constant detrending.
code: pe_dt <- detrendSignal(pe, type = "linear")

title: Signal Preprocessing Guide
text: known baseline period exists (e.g., pre-stimulus interval), can subtract baseline mean entire signal using removeBaseline().
code: pe_bl <- removeBaseline(pe, baseline_start = 0, baseline_end = 0.2)

title: Signal Preprocessing Guide
text: reproducible analysis, PhysioPreprocess supports pipelines chain multiple preprocessing steps together. Pipelines defined sequence named steps, specifying function arguments.

title: Signal Preprocessing Guide
code: pipeline <- createPipeline(   detrend = list(fn = "detrendSignals", method = "linear"),   filter  = list(fn = "butterworthFilter", low = 1, high = 40, type = "pass"),   notch   = list(fn = "notchFilter", freq = 50) ) print(pipeline)

title: Signal Preprocessing Guide
code: pe_processed <- applyPipeline(pe, pipeline, verbose = TRUE)

Previously operations silent, leaving gap provenance record. filtering behaviour changes.

title: PhysioPreprocess 0.3.0
text: IIR filtering core now runs compiled code (Rcpp). sosfilt(), lfilter(), zero-phase SOS path used butterworthFilter() (.sosfiltfilt) call C++ kernels implementing identical DF2T recursions; previous pure-R loops retained internally reference implementations covered numerical-parity tests (agreement ~1e-12 better). butterworthFilter() notchFilter() additionally process plain time x channels matrices single C++ call, parallelized across channels OpenMP available (thread count respects OMP_NUM_THREADS / OMP_THREAD_LIMIT). 64-channel, 5-minute, 256 Hz recording, default 1–40 Hz bandpass drops ~3.2 s ~0.07 s. notchFilter() ba-form (use_sos = FALSE) path butterworthFilter() now run compiled exact port signal::filtfilt() (identical zero-padding zero-state recursion; agreement signal::filtfilt() well within golden tolerances), also matrix-vectorized OpenMP-parallel. 50 Hz notch recording drops ~1.4 s ~0.08 s.

title: PhysioPreprocess 0.2.0
text: Initial release standalone package x-biosignal ecosystem, split monolithic PhysioExperiment codebase. PhysioPreprocess provides preprocessing operations physiological signal data held PhysioExperiment objects (SummarizedExperiment extension PhysioCore). operations write results new, named assay, leaving input data intact processing history preserved.

title: PhysioPreprocess 0.2.0
text: butterworthFilter() lowpass, highpass, bandpass, bandstop zero-phase (forward-backward) filtering. Uses second-order-sections (SOS) form default numerical stability high filter orders, fallback classic transfer-function form via use_sos. firFilter() zero-phase FIR filtering configurable window. notchFilter() power-line (50/60 Hz) noise removal, including harmonics, harmonics Nyquist skipped warned. filterSignals() moving-average smoothing detrendSignal() linear constant trend removal. resample() arbitrary target rate via linear, spline, FFT-based interpolation; decimate() integer-factor downsampling anti-aliasing lowpass filter; interpolate() integer-factor upsampling. assaySamplingRates() setAssaySamplingRate() track per-assay sampling rates assays resampled independently. EEG re-referencing via rereference(), supporting common average, single-channel, multi-channel (e.g. linked mastoids), REST fallback, optional removal reference channels. getCurrentReference() isAverageReferenced() query current reference recorded object metadata. detectBadChannels() (z-score, correlation, flatline criteria) interpolateBadChannels() (average position-weighted spline). detectArtifacts() continuous-data amplitude/gradient scanning automatic median + 5*MAD thresholding segment merging. rejectBadEpochs() baselineCorrect() epoched data. built-FastICA implementation (icaDecompose() / icaRemove()) stores components mixing matrices object, plus classifyICAComponents() flag artifact components kurtosis, autocorrelation, high-frequency power. fastICA-package backend (runICA() / removeICAComponents()). cleanData() chains bad-channel repair ICA artifact removal single call. Detrending baseline utilities: detrendSignals() (linear, mean, polynomial) removeBaseline() (window-based subtraction). Composable pipelines: createPipeline() builds PhysioPipeline named steps applyPipeline() runs sequence, print() method inspection.
